title: Attribution Statement Checker
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Educational Resources
description: Assess eight attribution statements by marking exactly which of five parts (title, author, source, license, change note) are missing.

learningObjectives: The learner will assess whether each of eight attribution statements is complete by identifying exactly which of the five checked parts are missing, with at least 7 of 8 judged correctly on the first attempt.
prerequisites: The terms attribution requirement, title, author, source, and license (TASL), and change note

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, commit an answer, and read the reason
keyQuestions: Which of the five parts are present?
commonMisconceptions: "CC BY" without a version is a complete license part
A copyright line with no license counts as credit
A change note is needed even when the work is unchanged
A site name is a source link
assessmentOpportunities: "Watershed Basics", link, licensed CC BY. What is missing?
Image courtesy of Maria Lopez. What is missing?
Is a change note needed for an unchanged copy?
Does a copyright line with no license count as credit?

controls.name: Title, Author, Source, License, Change note
controls.description: mark each part that is missing. A mark is a toggle, and a check badge shows it is on.

controls.name: None missing
controls.description: marks the statement as complete and clears the other marks.

controls.name: Check
controls.description: commits your answer and shows the correct set.

controls.name: Show definitions
controls.description: on a narrow screen the part definitions move behind this button.
